ms.report:
CDL library implementation
Three possible approaches were discussed in the Catalyst proposal to implement the Cardano domain-type serialization: code generation from CDDL to JavaScript/TypeScript, manual implementation or adapting the serialization code from the project cardano-js-sdk.
Even though at the time of writing the proposal and the Statement of Milestones, adapting cardano-js-sdk seemed to be the most promising path, during development it was apparent that this was not the best course of action. Therefore, this approach was dropped in favour of the code generation one.
The CDL project is composed of three parts:
・A code generator (located under conway-cddl/codegen).
・A set of YAML specifications derived automatically, but with manual additions and changes where necessary (available as YAML files under conway-cddl). These specify the structure of a Cardano transaction and are the basis for the code generation tool.
・The latest generated code and required runtime modules (available under src). This is the actual CDL library, as it will be installed in the final system.

Unit tests of CDL
There are two test suites for the Cardano Data Lite library, which can be found under tests/serialization and tests/api. Most relevant to Milestone 1 is the latter, which compares the type signatures of the methods provided by the CDL library to the ones provided by the latest garbage-collected version of Cardano Serialization Library, or CSL ("@emurgo/cardano-serialization-lib-nodejs-gc": "^12.1").
The API test suite located under tests/api can be run with the command ‘npm run test-api’. It shows that CDL's interface is mostly compatible with CSL. The test suite can test for:
・Missing classes: classes available in CSL but missing in CDL.
・Missing methods: methods available in CSL classes but missing in the equivalent CDL classes.
・Incompatible method signatures: methods with incompatible signatures in CDL compared to CSL. E.g: different return type, different number of param
